modes.cue_notes: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat. Let both knees fall to one side, allowing a gentle spinal rotation. Hold each side. Can also be done dynamically (sweeping knees side to side) as a transition or warm-up. For yin, hold each side passively and let the weight of the legs create the rotation.

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: A gentle lateral spinal rotation targeting the outer hip and IT band. The gallbladder meridian runs along the lateral body. Often used as a transition pose between supine postures or after deeper hip openers.
